imported.dcl-mcp-figma/src/guard: figma/src/guard (whole, keyless, on the library/ui layout)

changes: The Figma file key is never stored: it comes from the FIGMA_FILE_KEY environment variable, snapshot ingest strips it, generated headers, catalogs and the promotion manifest omit it, API errors redact it, and mappings name the file through the <DCL_FIGMA_FILE> placeholder. figma/key-guard.mjs enforces this.

Generation selects pages from the keyless generation inventory (figma-snapshot/generation-inventory.json) and skips retired pages and components per figma-snapshot/retirements.json; neither file, nor sync-state, carries a file key.

Paths follow library/ui; promote-reviewed writes components/<Name>/, components/assets, components/runtime and foundations/<family>/ instead of component-library/src/generated, and promotes only figma.config.json promotion.include plus their preview dependencies.

Review render signature resolves packages from pnpm node_modules instead of package-lock.json; the Cloudflare deploy (wrangler, _headers) and three unused styled-components Review helpers are removed; Review links to Figma were replaced by node ids.
Git LFS pointers fail loudly wherever the tooling hashes, parses or ships a file.

Upstream's frozen test capture (dcl-mcp-figma/test/fixtures/figma-snapshot) is not imported, because it stores the file key; figma/test/fixtures keeps this tree's keyless frozen capture, plus upstream's keyless test inputs (generation-inventory.json, pr38-sync-state.json) with the key dropped.

Supersession fails closed: a synced component replaces a hand-written one only when promotion.include names it explicitly (never as a preview dependency or through the all-eligible default); a pending or ineligible replacement fails promotion before anything is written. check-mappings skips components already in components/promotion.json, and an unmaterialized capture still fails it instead of falling back.

pull-live rejects a Colors swatch label that names the Figma file or its key before anything is staged, writes variables.json through the key-stripping sanitizer, and reports alpha before and after in colorChanges.

Pinned at 9c6dfbe6 (revision above), re-baselined from 0ec2a91 as one keyless import of the upstream sources plus the named deviations here, instead of a commit-by-commit replay. Snapshot inputs (8 changed, 3 new files) imported from 9c6dfbe6, key-stripped. References (PNGs and references.json) imported from figma-design-system 9c6dfbe6, sanitized; renders and fidelity.json generated locally by our review capture; Review generated code regenerated locally. The upstream-rendered legacy Footer evidence (Footer-0 and -1, FooterAccordion-0 to -3, FooterLink-0 to -3) is used by no Review case, reference record or consumer. By owner decision its 10 renders and 10 references are removed. The Review render signature hashes every reference image, so the evidence was recaptured in full after the removal: all 561 renders and fidelity cases came out byte-identical, only the signature changed, and the Review promotion manifest is resealed without the 20 files. Upstream's orphaned-assets.json is not imported (it accounts for upstream's generated Review).

Review capture teardown, the stalled-capture retry and the staged evidence publication are upstream's (capture-review.mjs, capture-retry.mjs, 9c6dfbe); this tree's earlier capture-teardown.mjs port is superseded behaviourally (keep-alive close, SIGTERM then SIGKILL, profile removal retried 10 times 200 ms apart), but its test coverage is lost upstream: capture-review.mjs is a top-level-await script, so no test can reach its teardown. Known gap, to be fixed upstream by extracting the teardown into a tested module and taken on the next port. Cases no longer covered: a browser that honours SIGTERM stops without waiting for the grace period; a hung browser is SIGKILLed; an already exited browser returns at once; profile removal is retried while a helper holds the profile; it fails loudly once the retries are spent; an error that waiting cannot fix is not retried; a real profile directory is removed. The capture checks Node against library/ui/package.json engines.node instead of a repository .node-version.

pull-live --page selects a page by id or unique name and keeps every other page's saved readiness (page-identity.ts, mergeSyncState); this tree's earlier name-based selection (nextSyncState) is superseded. A refresh must still contain every saved component unless it is retired (capture-completeness.ts).

The generator keeps Figma layer order over absolute layers and captures image fills as data URIs (4a94d9e). The Review playground drives the SearchBar through its Figma states (ebcc6a8), and the Review signature excludes the playground files, which audit mode never renders, while keeping the lockfile-based dependency signature.

Upstream's file-identity checks (records, inventory and sync state against config.fileKey) are removed: the tool works on the one file FIGMA_FILE_KEY names.

Generated components fail closed on a variant selection Figma never drew: pickView (figma/review/src/components/figma-view-state.ts) throws, naming the component and its axis values, instead of rendering the default view, in every environment and during server rendering (owner decision); interaction flags still fall back by dropping from the end, a boolean axis that is not true or false throws, and the runtime no longer takes a defaultKey. The caller's props reach FigmaView only as attributes={rest}, never spread over the generated configuration, and the runtime drops its own parameter names from them before the DOM. A component whose text overrides are not public (exposeTextSlots: false) lists them in a module constant passed as suppressed, which the runtime drops from attributes before the DOM, instead of binding them to unused aliases. The throw and the caller-prop boundary are local changes pending an upstream patch; exposeTextSlots and the suppression of private text props are a local deviation, upstream pending as FDS opt-in PR #4; the suppressed names are a frozen module constant the generator emits. Generation fails if a component's default selection is not a captured view (assertDrawnDefaults in src/generators/components.ts), so rendering with no props never throws; that guard is generic generator code, pending upstream in the FDS throw PR (step 2, after the variant contract).

Text roles are a local addition pending an upstream patch: figma.config.json components.<name>.textRoles binds a typed public prop to captured text layers by Figma node id, checked against the configured path of layer names (src/mappers/text-roles.ts). The raw capture reader accepts an optional node id, Figma's id verbatim: a partial variant drops the ids it inherits from the base tree, so a variant node has one only through its own set.id or replace, and a node without one is unbound, not an error, unless a role points at it. The mapper copies the id to the view node only to bind roles and then drops it, so ids never reach the spec, its hash or generated code; the generator types string roles as text and count roles as a number paired with a label prop, and names the link around a role's text with the href the role declares (never derived), and the runtime validates counts and names the enclosing action with the label. The capture records no descendant text ids yet, so the mechanism is exercised only by test fixtures and no component binds a role.

Generated styles use three cascade layers, a local change pending an upstream patch: dcl.reset (the runtime base styles), dcl.foundations (tokens and text styles) and dcl.components (component CSS), with the order statement repeated at the top of every generated stylesheet (src/generators/css-layers.ts). The runtime reset and the composed text styles are both zero-specificity :where() rules, so before this a bundle that loaded the runtime CSS after the text styles drew text in the inherited font. figma/review/test/runtime-cascade.test.ts checks the drawn font in Chromium under both orders. The Review renders are unchanged.

Ported from ad87b8e (#88), adapted to this tree's paint order: the views mapper emits no CSS gap for a non-wrapping SPACE_BETWEEN auto-layout and no negative-spacing overlap (margins, forced layer order) for any SPACE_BETWEEN one, because Figma ignores itemSpacing there and a CSS gap acted as a minimum that pushed NavBar controls far outside a 390px or 1024px root. Wrapped SPACE_BETWEEN frames keep their gap, as upstream does, until the capture records counterAxisSpacing. views-space-between.test.ts is upstream's, unchanged; this tree keeps overlap layer order in positionDecls rather than in overlapDecls, so the same SPACE_BETWEEN condition is applied there. Against the 2a050e3c Review, 98 gap declarations leave 12 component stylesheets and 20 renders (NavBar, NavMenuDropdown, WebTheme) move closer to their Figma references on every fidelity metric. A local fix pending an upstream patch: the runtime passes React keys on their own instead of inside spread props, which React 19 reported as an error.

Latent, not ported: 18ec19a's reversed overlap paint order. Upstream captures itemReverseZIndex and paints overlapping children last-to-first when it is set; this tree's capture does not record it and positionDecls always uses index+1. No captured frame sets it, so the generated output is identical today. Revisit when the capture records itemReverseZIndex.

Ported from 478f559 (#95), with the keyless part of e730fbc it builds on: check-scope.ts parses an aggregate's committed side with the base ownership and its staged side with the staged ownership (e730fbc's checkEntries baseOwnership and stagedOwnership parameters), and classifies each fidelity key once, by its committed entry when it has one, so staged ownership never frees a committed entry whose owner is null or uncaptured (478f559, verbatim). check-scope.test.ts takes 478f559's cases, adapted only to write their capture files through encodePageFileName, as this tree requires of every capture file name (windows-paths.test.ts). Control: without this commit its no-committed-owner case fails. No generated output or Review change.

The Figma capture and everything derived from its imagery leave this tree (owner decision): figma/figma-snapshot, the frozen test copy figma/test/fixtures/figma-snapshot, the Review evidence (references, renders, Figma icon exports, fidelity.json), the generated image-fill assets, references.json and promotion.json. Two pins: revision stays the code base the ported files and their deviations are compared against, and snapshot.revision is the capture commit. pnpm figma fetch-source (figma/src/sources/fds-source.ts) fetches the capture commit into a temporary repository, rewrites each capture file keyless (stripFileKey, stripImageMetadata, encodePageFileName, this tree's paths), overlays this tree's orphan ledger figma/ledger/orphaned-assets.json, and accepts the result only when it matches the snapshot digest table above; at 9c6dfbe6 it reproduces the removed capture byte for byte except pages.json, which differs only in how it escapes non-ASCII text, and orphaned-assets.json, which fetch-source takes from this tree, and regeneration from it changes nothing but the image fills. Generated components take imageFills from figma.config.json: the Review uses a neutral placeholder instead of an exported image fill. The Review is a gallery of the generated components; its icons render through the generated icon components. Relocated guard, both halves named: lock-digests.mjs fails on any tracked file under figma/ that differs from, is missing from or is not pinned in files; port-verification.mjs requires library/ui/port-verification.json, the record of the real-capture checks (fetch-source, diff, check-mappings, review-manifest, navbar-bounds) for this exact lock, FDS commit and figma/ tree, whenever the lock changes. figma diff, figma guard against the base, check-mappings, promotion-verify, review-manifest and review:check no longer run in this repository's CI; they run where the capture lives. Follow-up: figma-design-system CI publishes a verdict per candidate commit and replaces the local record. Removed with the evidence they produced or checked: capture-review.mjs, capture-scope.mjs (so the aad3791 port above no longer applies), capture-animations.mjs, check-evidence.mjs, check-review.mjs, review-signature.mjs, scripts/freeze-test-snapshot.mjs, capture-retry.mjs (the staged renders/fidelity publisher) and their tests; capture-browser.mjs (which now defines its own CaptureTimeout), browser-args.mjs and capture-teardown.mjs stay for the build checks. Promotion is reduced to its eligibility rule (figma/src/promotion/eligibility.ts, used by check-mappings): the seal, its verification, promote-reviewed, their mappings and scope modules, the CLI commands promotion-manifest, promotion-verify and promote-reviewed, the guard's seal check and their tests are removed, because their input lives in figma-design-system. Unit tests read the hand-written figma/test/fixtures/synthetic-snapshot.

figma/ledger/orphaned-assets.json is owned by this tree: it records which of this tree's own generated assets a recapture stopped referencing, so it describes dcl-one's output, not the capture, and figma-design-system's copy describes figma-design-system's output (its 58 entries name assets dcl-one never had). fetch-source overlays it into the cache; it may hold asset paths and hashes only, and the orphan guard checks it against this tree. retirements.json, which is capture identity, still comes from figma-design-system through the keyless transform.

Generated Review output (figma/review/src/generated and figma/review/src/review/catalog.json) is regenerated here by this tree's generator and figma.config.json from the pinned capture: it differs from figma-design-system's committed output wherever the ports above, the keyless context or the imageFills placeholder differ. figma diff against the fetched cache reports no change.

These files differed from figma-design-system at the code base before this pull request and are byte-identical to 67a95f89: earlier ports, the keyless form and this tree's layout. This pull request does not change them; listing each file's older reason is a follow-up.

Files with no counterpart in figma-design-system at the code base: this tree's own tooling (key guard, LFS prefetch, lock digests, port verification, fetch-source, check-build), its orphan ledger, its allowlists, the synthetic test capture and the tests built on it.

Live Figma access and capture ingest are removed: figma-design-system owns every read of Figma. Gone are pull-live and its automation modules, the REST source and its mappers, the Figma REST client, probe, the figma_screenshot MCP tool, the --source rest option, the capture-ingest and capture-merge commands with merge-component-chunks and split-icon-frames, the figma/capture plugin scripts and ingest-text-metrics, and their tests. The MCP tools that read the fetch-source cache stay. ingest-chunks and png-decode go too: strip-image-metadata keeps its own copy of the transport checksum, and its test proves byte equality instead of decoding. The key guard is the only reader of FIGMA_FILE_KEY: stripFileKey, stripFileKeyText and the CLI and MCP error text replace fileKey fields and Figma file URLs by pattern and read no environment, which also makes fetch-source's keyless transform independent of the environment. image-metadata-scan and its gate (figma/test/image-metadata.test.ts) stay: they check that no raster under library/ui/figma or in the public component assets carries non-rendering metadata, which covers product assets.

The gallery discloses what it does not provide: the catalog records, per component, how many image fills its generated stylesheet replaced with the neutral placeholder (counted from the generated CSS; a missing stylesheet fails the manifest), the component page states that those image fills are not provided and that the gallery makes no claim of visual parity, and the navigation says Figma image fills are not provided. review-notes.json, the per-component visual review statuses and findings the gallery displayed, is removed with the visual review it reported. Affected components: PlaceCard, SearchBar, NavBar, ProfilePic, NavNotificationsButton, NavProfileButton, NavNotificationItem, SearchResultItem, WebTheme, ShopModals, NavProfileMenu, WebThemeDarkMode, NavBarExplorer.

Owner decision: stored captures leave this tree, live Figma read access stays for local inspection. Restored from before the removal: the Figma REST client and token provider, the REST source and its mappers (their two helpers, download and svgProblem, now live in sources/rest-assets.ts because the live pull and chunk ingest stay removed), probe, `--source rest` for diff and the MCP read tools, figma_screenshot (the PNG is returned to the caller in memory, never written), and the env-only file-key readers (readFileKey, requireFileKey, redactFileKey), with error text redacting the key again. Shipped output comes from the pinned capture only: sync refuses the live source, figma_export_icons refuses to write live icons to disk, and no CI job runs live code or sets FIGMA_TOKEN. pull-live and the chunk ingest stay removed: they write captures. The verified-cache boundary: createApp requires snapshotLock unless a test opts out explicitly, sync and retire verify the cache before reading anything derived from it, and an unreadable marker or capture is an FdsCacheError; test fixtures carry their own lock and marker.

A capture marker that is not a JSON object is an FdsCacheError; the Figma token comes from the environment only, with no .env file; retire refuses a config whose snapshotDir is not the figma/figma-snapshot it reads; retirement writing stays (figma-design-system is retired after the POC) and runs only on a staged copy of a cache that runSync or retire verified first, proven by retirement-verified.test.ts.

Build verification observes browser network requests, including worker and frame targets, and rejects origin or prefix escapes and loading failures. Deviation codes must be own properties of the declared code table, so inherited Object prototype names cannot validate a port.

Build verification also checks the document the page ends on after each navigation, redirect or history change against the served origin and prefix, and Chromium error pages fail as failed requests; regression tests cover a redirect to a second origin that answers 200 and a history move outside the prefix. A deviation code declared as an own key of the code table validates. Build-check teardown attempts every step: a session that fails to close still releases the server, and the first error, from the check or else from teardown, is kept.
